detail.description: In `totalReserved` the accumulator was `acct` and is now `account_`, but it is a `number` (a running sum of `reservedMinor`), not an account. The rename faithfully preserves a pre-existing misnomer; it does not introduce a behaviour change, but the new name is arguably more misleading than the old one because it reads as a full `Account` value in a money-summing loop.

The trailing-underscore identifier `account_` is an unusual convention for this file — every other local (`row`, `res`, `key`, `amountMinor`) is plain camelCase, and the underscore exists only to avoid shadowing the `account` parameter. In `totalReserved`, the identifier `acct` was a numeric accumulator, not an account. Renaming it to `account_` makes a number read as an account object and is the only place the mechanical substitution degrades local meaning. Query shapes, table names, and mutation SQL are otherwise unchanged.

The summary claims a mechanical rename with "no behaviour change", but `reserve()` changed its funds check from `availableMinor(acct) < amountMinor` to `availableMinor(account_) < amountMinor - 1`. In `totalReserved` the accumulator (a `number`) is renamed from `acct` to `account_`, and in `loadAccount` (line 13) the pg `QueryResult` is likewise called `account_`. Neither is an `Account`; naming a numeric sum and a query result the same as the domain type (with a trailing-underscore convention that suggests a shadowed parameter) makes the file harder to read than before the rename and is exa

The Tasker's summary says "The existing suite passes" with no test added or cited. For a change touching `reserve`/`release`/`post` in a money path, a review cannot verify the "no behaviour change" claim from the summary alone — and here the claim was false.

The purportedly mechanical rename changes the insufficient-funds condition from `availableMinor(account_) < amountMinor` to `< amountMinor - 1`. An account with one minor unit less than the requested amount can now reserve funds, potentially persisting `reserved_minor > balance_minor`. This is not a mechanical rename. `reserve` changed `availableMinor(acct) < amountMinor` to `availableMinor(account_) < amountMinor - 1`, so a reserve of `available + 1` now succeeds. A zero-available account can reserve 1 minor unit; `reserved_minor` can exceed `balance_minor` and `availableMinor` goes negative. “The existing suite passes” after an insufficient-funds boundary change means the suite does not pin the reserve threshold, or the passing tests never exercised it. That is false confidence for a wallet mutation.
`totalReserved` renamed a numeric accumulator (`acct`) to `account_`. The identifier now looks like an `Account` and is a worse name than before.
